newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasolines jump after Texaco fire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasolines jump after Texaco fire.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline prices jumped at least one cent early Monday following news of a fire at Texaco's Los Angeles-area refinery, traders said.
The fire, which shut the plant's 9,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) alkylation unit, began at 1215 a.m. Pacific time (1515 EST/1015 GMT) and was still burning when West Coast trade opened at 0900 PST.
"It should affect gasoline, it shouldn't affect distillates," a broker said.
The affected unit helps make higher-octane gasoline for the plant, a company official said.
The plant's crude disillation capacity is 92,000 bpd.
January shipments of CARB-grade gasoline in Los Angeles were assessed 80/81 cents a gallon, up 2.75 cents a gallon from Friday's market. February shipments were a penny over January.
Conventional grade gasoline in L.A. rose about a cent to 77/78 cents a gallon on the refinery news.
Late last week, traders forecast flat to lower wholesale prices after heavy flooding in some parts of California lowered demand.
